findings.text: Provides a per CPU sample period for the lockup monitor derived from the hardware maximum frequency scaled to hertz and multiplied by the configured threshold, substituting a fixed five gigahertz fallback when the platform query reports zero.

Boot time predicate reporting whether counter based lockup detection can rely on true non maskable interrupts, with availability determined by the current interrupt mode of the performance monitoring unit.

Refresh on the calling CPU recomputes the detector period from threshold times hardware maximum; it does nothing when the platform reports no maximum and otherwise forwards the new period to the detector adjustment path.

Frequency policy observer ignores every event except creation of a new policy, then asks every CPU covered by that policy to refresh its own detector period without waiting, keeping the update ordered with global detector start and stop.

Clears one full page at the given destination, preferring a bulk memory operation sequence when toolchain and CPU support it, otherwise using cache line zeroing sized from a system register when allowed, falling back to paired zero stores.

Copies one full page from source to destination, preferring a bulk memory operation sequence when available, otherwise moving data with a loop of wide paired loads and paired non temporal stores covering the whole page.

User copy helpers report zero after moving the full requested length and otherwise report the count of trailing bytes not moved, with a fault path that reconciles partial progress and retries a single byte through an unprivileged access before computing the remainder.

Checksum over a byte buffer returns zero for nonpositive length and otherwise yields a folded sixteen bit result; it checks the range up front, tolerates unaligned ends by masking excess bytes around aligned accesses, accumulates with carry in wide arithmetic, folds to sixteen bits, and swaps bytes when the start is odd.

Computes the IPv6 pseudo header contribution by combining both sixteen byte addresses with length, protocol number and an incoming partial sum, then folding to the final sixteen bit value with endian dependent placement of the protocol byte.
Delay scaling turns microsecond and nanosecond intervals into loop counts with fixed round up factors and then into counter cycles using a jiffy based factor with a shift preserving precision.

Waits until the stable counter has advanced by the requested cycle count, first trying a deadline wait when timer wait instructions exist, else using event waits while far from expiry when that stream is available, always ending with a relaxed poll; the start stamp is taken with preemption held off.
Error injection helper redirects a probed kernel context to return at once by loading the saved program counter from the saved link register.
Encoding flag positions are 31 for the size flag and 22 for both the narrow branch flag and the twelve bit shift flag.
Address immediate layout spans two megabytes with a two bit low part; low mask covers the split width, high mask covers the remaining span, low field starts at bit 29 and high field at bit 5.
Fallback maximum CPU frequency used when the platform maximum is unknown is five gigahertz.

Branch and literal builders share a one megabyte reach with word scaled offsets and check kind, width, condition and range, yielding an architected fault encoding plus a diagnostic on violation; literal width uses one bit and compare branch width uses the size flag.

Load and store builders map size and access kind to base patterns then fill target, base, offset and immediate fields; they enforce width dependent alignment and signed range limits for immediates and pairs, limit atomics to 32 and 64 bit widths, encode ordering in dedicated bits, and yield a fault encoding on invalid input.

Creating a detector event at the same time as policy registration could leave the new event with the fallback period if refresh ran only on the notifying CPU; the design has each covered CPU refresh itself to close that window.
Checksum end handling reads whole words reaching past the caller range, relying on alignment that stays inside the same mapped extent plus an explicit up front check and masking of surplus bytes.
Delay start sampling runs with preemption held off to stay on one CPU, and frequency driven refreshes are dispatched per covered CPU so they order with global start and stop of the lockup monitors.

Fragments use but do not define three aggregates: a frequency policy exposing the set of covered CPUs, a notifier block exposing a callback member wired to the policy handler, and an IPv6 address exposing a sixteen byte array consumed as wide halves.
